target_customer: Foreign and underbanked workers who need to cash paychecks, send money home and spend with a card
problem: Underbanked workers pay high fees to cash checks and send remittances. Neema offers a digital wallet, debit card and cross border transfers without a bank account.
business_model: Payments fees on transfers and card use, later B2B payments infrastructure

founders.name: Barak Ben Ezer
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no background. Calcalist and Jerusalem Post pages found mention a co-founder, but names were not read in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a wallet, card issuing and cross border transfers needs licensing partners and compliance systems, but the engineering is standard fintech.

defensibility.rationale: Licenses and bank partnerships take time to obtain, and a niche of foreign workers in Israel is served with branches and community trust.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Banks became investors instead of rivals: Discount Capital in 2020 and Bank Hapoalim in late 2021.

market_need_then: The YC page cites 70 million underbanked Americans, and the company first served foreign workers in Israel who lacked ordinary bank accounts.

branding.name_origin: Swahili name meaning born into prosperity, per a Jerusalem Post profile seen in search results, also a common girls name in Africa

identity.voice_and_tone: positioned as Better than a Bank

branding.brand_signature: Better than a Bank tagline and a flagship branch per launch country
branding.community_and_virality: A co-founder says each launch country gets a flagship branch for branding and education.

brand_strength.rationale: Name fits the audience and the brand carries partnerships with Mastercard and Alipay, but no brand specific data exists.

outcome_analysis: Neema is active, not failed. It served foreign workers in Israel, took money from Discount Capital in 2020 and Bank Hapoalim in late 2021, and in 2026 signed a Mastercard partnership. The YC Inactive status appears stale. The CEO named in 2026 is Moshe Kimhi, not the YC listed founder.
notes: Company site fetch returned only a page title. The 2020 Discount Capital deal was NIS 5.25M at a NIS 28.5M pre-money valuation per Globes; no USD figure is recorded. The 2021 Hapoalim figure was reported as a plan to invest $10M at a $40M to $50M valuation (Calcalist). Startupim claims an $18M Series C led by Kima Ventures in December 2021 and Bouncewatch lists ILS 55M; both are single aggregator claims, so the round size is unresolved. CB Insights total $10.27M versus Startupim $20.62M. Competitors: the only competitor search returned no 2017 sources, so the list is empty. Founded 2015 per Calcalist; Preqin says 2013.
